Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original HAND-DRAWN industrial mecha concept-development sheet on ivory drafting paper, 1536x1024 landscape. Match input image 1, the GUIHANG mother ship master, as the authoritative exterior visual identity. Warm-white armor, slate blue-gray structure, graphite recesses, sparse brick-red identification, amber work lights. Crisp pencil/ink contour, light construction lines, controlled marker shadows. No photoreal CGI, no fantasy monument, no generic new ship or copied franchise, no fake dimension numbers, no unreadable handwritten paragraphs. These are concept views, not validated engineering projections. Preserve low bridge aft of center, short faceted bow, thick enclosed body, TWO port-side midship mouths separated by one thick pier (forward LAUNCH, aft RECOVERY), six aft engine apertures total in two columns of three, only short fins. Small figures in the reference are schematic, not exact scale evidence.
Asset: coherent six-view concept sheet of this SAME ship, not six alternatives. Layout top two rows each with two long horizontal ship views; bottom row with two end views and generous blank margins. Labels only PORT, STARBOARD, TOP, BOTTOM, BOW, STERN.
PORT: bow left, stern right, BOTH rectangular side service mouths visibly open at the midship waist, bridge in same aft position and three visible near-bank nozzles.
STARBOARD: mirror longitudinal orientation with bow right, stern left; opposite side is plated service access with CLOSED rectangular maintenance panels, no invented open garden or symmetric active hangar.
TOP: bow left and stern right, one central longitudinal spine, paired shoulder masses, compact low bridge, near-side hangar recess corresponding to PORT. BOTTOM: bow left and stern right, reinforced keel and maintenance hatches; no bridge and no duplicated dorsal details.
BOW: short faceted nose facing directly toward viewer, broad shoulder silhouette behind it and tiny centered bridge silhouette above; NO engine holes at the nose.
STERN: directly behind, exactly SIX main nozzles as two vertical columns of THREE circles; structure between columns, tiny bridge above. Do not turn them into four or eight.
All views in restrained mostly orthographic drawing language, no extreme perspective, line weight separates primary silhouette from panel detail. Keep the same bow slope, hull beam, bridge location, port longitudinal position and engine count across ALL views. Fill the page elegantly without overlap. Do not add decorative inset shapes or extra views.

Asset: clear hull decomposition and internal zoning CONCEPT study for the SAME mother ship.
Upper 60 percent: three-quarter EXPLODED ASSEMBLY drawing of the vessel with its coherent graphite structural backbone continuous. Lift only the major warm-white external armor sections slightly away with dotted guide lines: forward protection/nose cap, preserved-community compartment shells, central dorsal cover, port hangar shoulder cover, aft power cover. Keep both launch/recovery mouths together as a single side assembly. Aft complete engine assembly remains SIX nozzles, two columns of three. Explosion is modest and readable, not a cloud of random parts. Inner functional modules are large architectural volumes, not fully engineered reactors.
Lower 40 percent: same ship in PORT-side longitudinal CUTAWAY, bow left stern right. Clearly separate seven zones in this order and with tiny English labels only: SHIELD at bow, PRESERVATION with isolated sleeping/seed compartments forward, HABITAT inside protected midbody, HANGAR on port side of that region, INDUSTRY aft of habitats, POWER well aft, DRIVE at stern.
HABITAT is an ENCLOSED rotating-drum candidate INSIDE the hull, longitudinal axis, located inward and toward starboard from the port hangar. Show its curved residential decks as an internal module, not an enormous ring sticking out of the exterior or a floating garden. Central service spine is nonrotating. Hangar side module occupies a DISTINCT volume, not drawn through the residential drum. Show a simple separation between life/preservation systems and aft power volume. Front preserved-community blocks have redundancy, not one fragile glowing crystal.
Keep the open twin side bays in the same place as the exterior and the bridge small. Use lightly differentiated muted tints for zones and solid simple structural interfaces. No energy magic, no giant fuel flames, no arbitrary rooms whose scale pretends to be validated. Show how the parts relate; no numerical measurements.

Input image 2 defines ORIGINAL shipborne machines: small nonhumanoid EXPLORER, armored humanoid SENTINEL, four-arm HARVESTER. Match their form family.
Asset: a hand-drawn HANGAR and PORT OPERATIONS design sheet, NOT a new exterior design.
Upper left dominant 60 percent: interior perspective looking from the aft maintenance gallery toward the port-side hull with TWO separate exterior openings visible, forward LAUNCH and aft RECOVERY, separated by a thick fixed pier. Through each opening is dark space without a giant planet. Put the humanoid in a supported launch cradle by one lane; put a folded four-arm harvester in the separate capture/inspection area, not blocking the launch lane. Clearly show outer service alcove, smaller machine transit throat, inner doors and their side parking pockets. Rails and clamp arms have actual mounting points. The machine is large relative to a HUMAN worker, at least ten times their height; humans only inside small PRESSURIZED service boxes behind windows, or in visibly tethered pressure suits. No casual people standing in vacuum, no stools or houseplants in open hangar.
Bottom left: one very simple TOP-DOWN block layout. Exterior/space is to left, interior maintenance to right. Two parallel routes through two separate gates: outgoing LAUNCH arrow to left, incoming RECOVERY arrow to right. Capture and unload sit only on the incoming line; shared transfer gallery at rear has a clear stop point, not overlapping through-traffic. Do not point both arrows outwards.
Right column: exploded detail of ONE sliding port-door module: outer frame attached to hull, thick sliding leaf displaced into its adjacent recessed pocket, guide mechanism, inner fixed capture saddle with paired locks, and service umbilical kept disconnected until capture. Small second inset shows the same door CLOSED flush. Only minimal labels LAUNCH / RECOVERY / SERVICE / DOOR MODULE / CLOSED.
Lighting concentrated on clamps and active lanes; some service bays dark and sealed. Show pressure boundaries as thick glass and local small airlocks, not a giant repeatedly pressurized hangar. No blueprint dimension claims, no free-floating parts except explicit exploded inset.
